change.title: ao-replay/8832
change.description: perf(chat): open and switch chats without waiting on workspace reads
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

findings.title: Paths endpoint offers files deleted from the worktree but still in the index
findings.body: The old client built the @-mention list from `/workspace/files` and dropped `status === "deleted"` entries, with the comment "A deleted path cannot be read, so offering it would insert a reference the agent then fails to resolve" (removed from `useConversation.ts`). The new endpoint takes its inventory from `workspacePaths`, which runs `git ls-files -z -co --exclude-standard` (`workspace_files.go:1806`). `-c` lists every index entry whether or not the file still exists on disk, so a tracked file removed with plain `rm` (an agent does this routinely) is listed. `workspaceSourcePaths` never checks status or existence. It only reads `changes` when `total > limit`, and then it adds deleted paths from `changedPaths()` (`workspace_files.go:1857`) and does not filter them. The menu therefore offers unreadable paths again, silently. The doc comment on `WorkspaceFilePaths` says it lists "the files ListWorkspaceFiles lists", but that endpoint also marks these as deleted. Drop deleted paths before returning them, for example by checking `changes.statuses[rel] == WorkspaceFileDeleted` or with an `lstat`. The `git ls-files -d` list is another option. Whichever you pick, the paths read in the non-truncated branch need it too. The fallback in `fetchWorkspaceFilePaths` does filter deleted, so the two routes now disagree.

findings.title: Deletion test only covers a staged `git rm`, which hides the unstaged-delete case
findings.body: `TestListWorkspaceFilePathsMatchesFullListWithoutDeletions` removes the file with `git rm`, which also removes it from the index, so `git ls-files -co` never returns it and the assertion passes. A file deleted from disk and still in the index (` D`) is the case the old client filter handled, and nothing here covers it. The helper `listedPaths` also filters by `Status != WorkspaceFileDeleted`, so a test with an unstaged delete would fail against the current implementation. Add that case. Test the capped branch too, where `changedPaths()` re-adds deleted paths.

findings.title: `fetchWorkspaceFilePaths` was inserted between `useWorkspaceFilePaths` and its doc comment
findings.body: The block comment "Every path in the session worktree, for @-mention completion…" (lines 2216-2224) now sits above `fetchWorkspaceFilePaths`, and `useWorkspaceFilePaths` (line 2240) has no doc. The comment also still says the daemon serves this list from the full workspace listing, which is no longer true now that it uses `/workspace/paths` with a fallback. Move the comment back above the hook and describe the fallback on the new function.

contracts.action: New GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/paths returning visible file paths only
contracts.equivalent_path: GET /workspace/files (listWorkspaceFiles) at backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:1141, backed by ListWorkspaceFiles at backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go:294
contracts.before_after: The old path resolves compare/status/diff for every file, builds summaries, and the client filtered out deleted files. The new path lists `git ls-files` through the shared path cache and skips status unless the list exceeds the cap. It does not drop deleted-but-indexed paths, so the two differ for unstaged deletions.
contracts.visible_effect: The @-mention menu is filled from this list, so an unstaged-deleted file would appear as a mention candidate.
contracts.failure_mode: Unknown session: `envelope.WriteError` gives 404. Nil `Svc` gives 501. A git failure gives 500. An older daemon answers `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`, handled by the client fallback.

contracts.action: SearchWorkspaceFiles now searches paths from workspaceSourcePaths (cap 20000) and builds a summary only for the returned page
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous implementation filtered ListWorkspaceFiles().Files (cap 5000) and read every summary
contracts.before_after: Before: one full listing including git state, with errors from workspaceGitState turning into a degraded result. After: path inventory plus per-hit resolveWorkspaceChanges (cached) and a stat. It never calls workspaceGitState, so a git-state failure no longer matters for search. Scratch workspaces reuse scratchWorkspaceFiles.
contracts.visible_effect: Search can reach files past the old 5000 cap. Result fields (status, size, binary, fingerprint) are computed the same way as the full list, which the new tests check.
contracts.failure_mode: An error in resolveWorkspaceChanges or a path with no owning worktree returns an error for the whole search instead of skipping that hit.

contracts.action: fetchWorkspaceFilePaths falls back to /workspace/files when the paths route answers ROUTE_NOT_FOUND
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous inline GET of /workspace/files in useWorkspaceFilePaths and NewChatPage
contracts.before_after: The old code made one call and filtered deleted files. The new code calls the paths route first and on ROUTE_NOT_FOUND (api.go:465) makes the old call with the same filter. The signal is passed to both. NewChatPage now uses clientForSessionHost(hostId), which resolves to apiClient or the host client as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Remote hosts running an older daemon still get a menu. Hosts on a new daemon get the lighter response.
contracts.failure_mode: Any other error is returned as-is and thrown through recordWorkspaceResult (workspace missing/recovery handling) in the hook. NewChatPage throws it into the query error. A rejected fetch propagates as a query error.

contracts.action: The file-path query is enabled only after the composer reports an @ query (onFileQuery)
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: enabled whenever the snapshot existed and the session did not need resume
contracts.before_after: `fileMenuAsked` is local state set by the ChatComposer effect that fires whenever the trigger is a file trigger (ChatComposer.tsx:864-867). Once set it stays set for the life of the component.
contracts.visible_effect: No workspace read happens on opening a chat. The first @ shows no menu until the fetch returns, because filePaths is [] until then. After that the menu fills in, since suggestions depend on filePaths.
contracts.failure_mode: If the fetch fails there is no menu and no message. This matches the earlier behaviour, where the error was only recorded.

contracts.action: Route loader prefetches the conversation for a cached local chat session
contracts.equivalent_path: useConversation's own infinite query on mount
contracts.before_after: The prefetch uses conversationQueryOptions(sessionId) with the local key. It is skipped when data is cached, when no trusted base URL exists, or when the session is not a local non-cloud chat that has no pending resume. The hook query uses staleTime Infinity and refetchOnMount false, so a prefetched result is reused on mount.
contracts.visible_effect: The chat's first page loads in parallel with the SessionView chunk.
contracts.failure_mode: The prefetch is fire-and-forget (`void`), so a rejection leaves the query in error state in the cache. The mounting hook then reads it as an error or refetches. I did not check which. `useConversation.ts` is outside this part's diff.
contracts.open_question: Does a prefetch that fails leave useConversation showing an error or empty state instead of retrying when SessionView mounts?

contracts.action: SessionView no longer invalidates the workspaces query when a chat view is activated
contracts.equivalent_path: The same effect's conversation invalidation just below it, and other workspaceQueryKeyForHost invalidations at SessionView.tsx:508
contracts.before_after: Before: first successful chat-view POST invalidated both the conversation (if unsettled) and the local workspaces list. After: only the conversation. The test was updated to assert that workspaces is not invalidated.
contracts.visible_effect: Opening a chat no longer refetches the session list. A stale session summary (for example a woken session whose needsResume flag has cleared) is corrected only by events or other invalidations.
contracts.failure_mode: If a wake emits no workspace change event, the list could stay stale. The new comment says a wake emits no event for the sleep marker, but I did not read the event code.
contracts.open_question: Does anything else refresh the workspaces list after a chat view wakes a sleeping session, now that this invalidation is gone?

summary: The new /workspace/paths endpoint and the reworked search are mostly sound, and the OpenAPI spec, schema.ts and DTO changes are in sync. One real regression: the endpoint lists tracked files that were deleted from disk but not staged. The old client filtered those out of the @-mention menu, and the new test does not cover that case because it uses `git rm`. There is also a detached doc comment in `useConversation.ts`. Two behaviours I could not fully settle: the chat prefetch's failure behaviour, and whether the removed workspaces invalidation in `SessionView.tsx` leaves the list stale after a wake.
